incidente.resumo: During a periodic update of the list of sites flagged as harmful, the URL '/' was mistakenly checked in as a value to the file; since '/' expands to all URLs, every Google search result showed the warning "This site may harm your computer". The on-call site reliability team found the problem and reverted the file.

descricao.texto: In an update to the list of sites flagged as installing malicious software, the URL '/' was mistakenly checked in as a value to the file, and '/' expands to all URLs; the authors describe this as human error.
trechos: Google flags search results with the message "This site may harm your computer" if the site is known to install malicious software in the background or otherwise surreptitiously.
We maintain a list of such sites
We periodically update that list and released one such update to the site this morning.
Unfortunately (and here's the human error), the URL of '/' was mistakenly checked in as a value to the file and '/' expands to all URLs.

passos.texto: The on-call site reliability team reverted the file.

acoes.texto: Planned: investigate the incident and put more robust file checks in place to prevent it from happening again.
trechos: We will carefully investigate this incident and put more robust file checks in place to prevent it from happening again.

Since we push these updates in a staggered and rolling fashion, the errors began appearing between 6:27 a.m. and 6:40 a.m. and began disappearing between 7:10 and 7:25 a.m., so the duration of the problem for any particular user was approximately 40 minutes.

observacoes: The date comes from the publication date in the text (1/31/2009) and the post's statement that the problem happened 'this morning'. The opening paragraph gives a window of 6:30 a.m. to 7:25 a.m. PST; the stated per-user duration of approximately 40 minutes is used. The text does not say how the problem was first noticed, only that the on-call site reliability team found it. categoria_causa is human-error: the text describes the cause as an operator action (a value mistakenly checked in) with no separate pre-existing condition, which the prompt's operator-action rule classifies as human-error; configuration-error was also considered because the wrong value sits in a list file.
